text.p: Western Resources Inc said Kansas City Power & Light Co shareholders who rejected a proposed merger with UtiliCorp United Inc showed support of the Western Resources merger offer.

It said Thursday a preliminary vote showed 46.9 percent of Kansas City Power shares voting at an August 16 shareholder meeting voted for the proposed UtiliCorp/Kansas City Power merger compared with 53.1 percent voting against or abstaining on the proposal.

"There is only one offer on the table now, and it is the one that offers $31 per share and a dividend increase up to 45 percent over Kansas City Power's current dividend," said Western Resources chairman John Hayes Jr in a statement.
Hayes said Western Resources would continue on its course to have Kansas City Power holders tender their shares. Its offer runs through October 25, unless further extended.
Meanwhile, Kansas City Power said Thursday its board had rejected Western Resources' hostile exchange offer and continued to recommend that shareholders not tender shares to Western.
